nodes.name: Kart drive controller
nodes.purpose: Per-update throttle, steering, drive force, grip and velocity integration for every kart on the course

nodes.name: Kart stat tables
nodes.purpose: Data tables that give each kart its top speed, acceleration curve, friction, gravity, hop impulse and handling multiplier

nodes.name: Drift and hop
nodes.purpose: The hop that opens a drift, the charge tiers accumulated while drifting and the mini-turbo paid back on release

nodes.name: Kart effect handlers
nodes.purpose: Timed kart states: boosts from items and ramps, spin-outs and their recovery, and the out-of-bounds retrieval sequence

nodes.name: Chase camera
nodes.purpose: Third-person chase camera that lags position and look target behind the kart, leans into a drift and steps its follow distance with speed effects

nodes.name: Item actors and hits
nodes.purpose: World-space item actors and the per-player hit test that turns a touch into a trigger

nodes.name: Item window roulette
nodes.purpose: HUD item window that cycles icons, rolls a result from a rank-indexed curve and reveals the held item

nodes.name: Race loop and start
nodes.purpose: Frame loop that runs the kart simulation in fixed substeps and the start sequence that releases karts onto the course

cards.name: Throttle acceleration
cards.summary: Speed-banded acceleration curve with a hard cap on horizontal velocity
cards.behavior: With the throttle held, the kart adds the ten-entry acceleration value for its current band, where each band spans a tenth of the kart's top speed, so the kart climbs fastest from a standstill and slowly near the top of its range. The race build scales the first seven bands by 3.2 and the last three by 2.8; an alternate path used during scripted states leaves the entry unscaled but adds a slope term. Current speed is floored at zero after every step. The integrated velocity is then clamped so its horizontal magnitude never exceeds 9.0, scaling all three components down together when it would.

cards.name: Top speed by engine class
cards.summary: Per-kart top speed chosen by engine class, bundled with the acceleration curve and body radius
cards.behavior: Each kart slot owns one entry in five top-speed rows selected by engine class: the slowest row sits near 290, the two middle rows near 310 and near 320, the extra row near 310 and the battle row at 245. Spawning also copies a ten-entry acceleration curve, a friction scalar of 5800, a gravity scalar of 2600 and a body radius of 5.5 or 6.0. Top speed is a target for the drive model rather than a wall on its own, since the separate horizontal magnitude cap is what finally bounds motion; the drive model pins current speed back to top speed whenever an accelerator step would overshoot it.

cards.name: Steering rate against speed
cards.summary: Steering authority falls with speed and is gated by a resistance that sets how fast the kart yaws
cards.behavior: The stick value is filtered for a dead zone and held as a 16.16 fixed-point steer position that chases the input instead of snapping to it. Steering works only above a scaled speed of 15; below that both resistance values are fixed at 8. Above it the resistance is chosen from the direction the stick is already travelling: 15 when the change is small and in the turning direction, 5 and 9 for large and small changes against it, and 3 and 6 when no turn is registered. A drift adds 3 to each base, being under the out-of-bounds or fluid level multiplies the resistance by 1.5 and merely passing that level by 1.2. The resulting yaw rate divides the steer position by 8 plus current speed over 50, or by 8 while drifting, and is scaled by 1.5 outside a drift. Turning also scrubs speed: 0.01 per yaw degree normally and 0.004 while drifting. Every kart then multiplies the final yaw by a handling multiplier of 1.15 to 1.28.

constants.name: turnScrubPerDegree
constants.unit: speed units per yaw degree per update

constants.name: driftTurnScrubPerDegree
constants.unit: speed units per yaw degree per update

cards.name: Drift charge tiers
cards.summary: Holding a drift against the turn charges a tier that is later cashed in as a mini-turbo
cards.behavior: While the kart is drifting, the charge counter rises by at most one per update and raises the drift tier every time it passes 18, up to three tiers. After each tier the counter floor moves to 10, so later tiers arrive sooner, and a fresh drift starts from zero. Pushing the stick far against the drift instead drives the counter toward 100 and holds the tier, and holding that outward charge at 100 bleeds 4.0 of speed per update. The charge is erased if the drift ends first, and the drift timer itself saturates at 100 so a long drift cannot bank more than its tiers. Drifting scales the yaw rate by 0.65, or 0.9 when the drift is pushed outward.

cards.name: Drift hop and mini-turbo
cards.summary: The hop that opens a drift and the boost that closes it
cards.behavior: A drift opens with a hop: vertical velocity starts at 0.93 and a jerk of 0.03 pulls acceleration negative every update so the rise decelerates, while gravity is forced to 500 for the hop. Hop acceleration is clamped to plus or minus 9 and hop velocity to 15, and the hop is over once velocity reaches zero. An ordinary grounded update also loses 0.02 of vertical position, which is what keeps the kart settling onto the surface. Releasing a drift charged to tier two or better sets a mini-turbo flag that ramps an extra 580 of drive force in at 0.2 per update and clears it after 0x1F updates; the flag cannot be set again while it is active.

cards.name: Off-road grip and drag
cards.summary: Grip and drive force fall away on loose surfaces and as speed climbs
cards.behavior: With both rear tyres on the asphalt the kart recovers its lateral velocity with a 0.925 coefficient. On any other surface the coefficient comes from a speed-indexed row that starts at 0.825 and falls through 0.8, 0.725, 0.625 and 0.425 to a floor of 0.3 from the sixth band up; the band is the scaled speed divided by 10 and capped at 10, so a fast kart on a loose surface slides instead of gripping. Drive force is reduced in the same conditions: each contacting tyre adds a per-surface term, 0.09 for a loose surface on three wheels and 0.03 on the fourth, and the sum is subtracted as a fraction of the drive force. Every update also subtracts 0.12 times the kart's 5800 friction from velocity and divides the difference by 6000 to produce the step.

constants.name: looseSurfaceResistanceRear
constants.unit: drive force fraction per contacting tyre

constants.name: looseSurfaceResistanceFront
constants.unit: drive force fraction per contacting tyre

cards.name: Ramp and item boosts
cards.summary: Ramps and the mushroom item both pin speed to top speed while a boost meter drains
cards.behavior: A boost pad sets current speed to the kart's top speed and raises a boost power toward 400 at 0.01 per update while the kart is on the ramp surface or airborne. When the power falls to 1 or less the effect ends, and a kart that spent more than 0x33 updates airborne on the way out has its speed multiplied by 0.7 and its stored speed term scaled the same way. The wooden ramp variant pins speed to the slowest class row, raises power toward 300 at 0.1 and halves speed when it expires. The mushroom item instead sets a timer of 0x50 updates, raises power toward 400 at 0.5 per update, and lets it decay at 0.1 once the timer is spent. Both ramps also override kart gravity, to 3500 and 1800, for as long as the effect lasts.

cards.name: Rocket start and burnout
cards.summary: Where the throttle is pressed inside the countdown decides between a launch boost and a spin-out
cards.behavior: During the start sequence the throttle still adds the banded acceleration value but on a shortened curve, at 3.0 for the first six bands and 2.5 for the last four, so karts build speed before the release. The first throttle press records the race frame counter. If the throttle goes down within 8 updates of that moment in a normal race, or within 0x14 updates in a time trial, a start-boost trigger is queued that hands out a 0x0050-update boost. Pressing the throttle too late, or reaching 0.9 of top speed without the boost queued, queues a spin-out instead. The burnout spins the kart at 2 degrees per update through two phases and then 1 degree per update until it has turned 180 degrees, and divides speed by 3 when it ends.

constants.name: substepsPerFrame
constants.unit: kart simulation substeps per rendered frame

cards.name: Item box roulette
cards.summary: Icon cycle, rank-weighted roll and reveal of the held item
cards.behavior: Collecting a box starts the item window, which slides in at 4 units per update to 0x40 before it begins cycling. The cycle runs in three passes: icons 1 to 0x0F stepping by one with a delay of 2 updates per icon over two passes, then icons 1 to 6 with a delay of 8, then icons 1 to 4 with a delay of 0x10, after which the real result is rolled and the window animates to it. The roll draws a random number below 100, mixes it with controller noise and the race frame counter modulo 100, and uses that index into a 100-entry stretch of a curve picked by the player's rank, so each rank sees its own distribution. In a single-player grand prix a further roll below 0x51 decides between a real item and an empty result. A spent box waits 20 updates, is pushed back to its reset height minus 20 and then rises 0.45 per update to rest 8.66 above its origin.

cards.name: Shell projectile
cards.summary: Held, aimed and launched shell that falls, bounces and can be thrown backwards
cards.behavior: A held shell is placed in front of the kart by transforming a local offset through the kart's orientation matrix, sitting behind the nose by the kart radius plus the shell radius plus 2. Pressing the item button with the stick pushed back past -0x2D launches it forward at 1.2 times kart speed, or at 8 when the kart is slower than that. Pressing without the stick pushed back first swings the shell out to the side through a 170 degree arc at 20 degrees per update and launches it when the arc completes. In flight the shell loses 0.5 of vertical velocity per update down to a floor of -2, spins at 10 degrees per update, and is collided against the terrain each update with a radius of 4 so walls bounce it. A shell that has struck a kart falls under 0.3 gravity for the remaining life of its timer. Three shells orbit their parent at a radius of 8.

cards.name: Banana hazard
cards.summary: Dropped or thrown peel that spins out a kart which is not shielded
cards.behavior: A held peel follows the kart at a fixed trailing offset. Dropping it starts a 0x00B4-update arming window during which it stays harmless to the kart that dropped it. Throwing it forward gives it 0.75 times kart speed plus 3.5 plus a term from how far the stick is pushed, or 4 when the kart is barely moving. In flight it loses 0.15 of vertical velocity per update down to a floor of -1 and settles onto the ground when the terrain pushes back, staying armed until something touches it. On contact the peel plays a fall under 0.3 gravity clamped at -5 and is removed. The victim takes a full spin when the steering input is 20 or more either way, when scaled speed is 30 or less, when the kart is airborne, or when a non-human kart is not already losing; otherwise only a wobble is applied.

cards.name: Spin-out and recovery
cards.summary: Multi-turn spin driven by a step table, then a recovery that restores the saved heading
cards.behavior: A spin-out clears the steering state, saves the heading and starts a step index of 2. Every update the kart yaws by the table entry for the current index, drawn from a five-entry table of 6, 6, 12, 9 and 10 degrees, and the accumulated yaw is measured against a full 0x168 turn; the index drops each time a full turn completes and the effect ends when the index falls below zero. Speed bleeds while the spin runs: a human kart loses 1.0 per update, a non-human kart loses 4.0 and then another 30, and an instant spin-out loses 100 at once. Recovery restores the saved heading and zeroes steer, and a human kart still holding an active rapid-throttle boost keeps at least 90 of speed for the whole spin while its boost timer is refreshed.

cards.name: Out-of-bounds retrieval
cards.summary: Lift, fade and return of a kart that leaves the course or falls below the surface
cards.behavior: A kart whose body sits below the local surface height while more than 600 units from the terrain is marked for retrieval. A lift counter runs up to 0x3C while the kart is held, then the kart is raised toward 100 above the surface at 0.012 per update until it has cleared 40, at which point it fades out 8 per update. Once the alpha passes 0xF0 the kart is placed back on the nearest track path and faded in 8 per update, creeping down to 2 above its ground height at 0.04 per update. At three counter values it is nudged 10 units along its heading, at 0xFC it is snapped to the first point of the track path, and at 0x5B it is released from the hold. A released kart still at 0.9 of its top speed is spun out.

cards.name: Chase camera follow
cards.summary: Camera position and look target trail the kart with separate horizontal and vertical blend rates
cards.behavior: The chase camera keeps a look target and a position and each update moves both a fraction of the way toward a point built from the kart's position and orientation. Horizontal position blends at 0.15 and the look height at 0.5, while the camera's own height blends at only 0.15 so it rides a hop slowly; during a low-speed hop those vertical blends drop to 0.01 and 0.02. Camera yaw is swept toward the kart heading by a step limited to 500 units unless a spin, a hit, a burnout or a wall contact makes it hold the last angle instead. While drifting the camera yaw offset is driven to 12 degrees, or 0x0B60 units when the drift is pushed outward. The final camera point is collision tested with a radius of 3.

cards.name: Camera pull-back
cards.summary: Speed effects push the follow distance out from its base and step it back down
cards.behavior: The follow distance is one scalar pulled toward a target of the base distance plus an effect term, moving one unit per update and clamped so it never overshoots. Each effect term has its own approach rate: a drag or launch adds 20 at 0.2 per update, a boost adds 8 at 0.2, an airborne ramp launch adds 20 at 0.1, a squash adds 25 at 1.0 and a spin-out adds 18 at 0.2. When the effect ends the term counts down by one or two per update and the entry is cleared once it reaches zero. One mode forces the term to 40 outright, and the base distance itself depends on the view mode, at 40 for the single-screen view and 60 for the wider modes.

cards.name: Draft behind another kart
cards.summary: Sitting in the wake of a kart ahead long enough adds drive force
cards.behavior: A kart travelling at a scaled speed of 50 or more tests every other live kart once per update: a triangle reaching 70 units ahead of the tester, 10 degrees either side of its heading, with a near edge only 10 units out at 40 degrees, decides whether the other kart is inside the wake. Each update with a kart inside the wake adds one to a counter, and reaching 0x3D raises a draft flag that ramps an extra 580 of drive force in at 0.01 per update for a human kart. While the flag is up the counter ticks down and the flag clears at zero; the counter is also reset whenever no kart is in the wake or the tester drops below the speed threshold.
